title: Minimax Rates for the Two-Period G-Formula Mean under Transition Smoothness
banked_reason: D0 mathematics is sound, but D0.5 found field novelty unmet: the incoming r1 lower rate embeds Robins et al. (2009) Theorem 3.1, while the upper and lower rates remain unmatched.
gap_reasons: The proved nonmatching first-order bracket does not establish a field-level advance.
The incoming r1 floor is a legal embedding of Robins et al. (2009), Theorem 3.1; variation dependence does not block transfer.
The upper and lower rates remain unmatched, so the minimax rate and sharp elbow remain open.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 proved a qualified incoming-transition lower channel, a standard terminal channel, and a computable nonmatching first-order upper bound, including a connected rough-transition subclass outside Robins et al. (2016) condition (c2). The field claim collapsed because the incoming lower rate transfers from Robins et al. (2009), while no attaining higher-order estimator was proved. A future retry must close the upper-rate gap rather than rederive r1.
tldr:
For the two-decision g-formula target \(\psi=E[Y(1,1)]\), the note proves a computable cross-fitted first-order upper bound and three converse floors. The honest bracket is
\[
\max\{n^{-1/2},n^{-r_1},n^{-r_2}\}\lesssim\mathfrak R_n(\mathcal M)\lesssim n^{-1/2}+n^{-(\gamma_1+\gamma_t)}+n^{-(\gamma_2+\gamma_b)},
\]
under the stated nonemptiness and converse-slack qualifications. The incoming lower channel pairs the first propensity with incoming-state transition smoothness; the terminal channel is the familiar single-time-type component. The auxiliary monotone-MAR comparator is now a complete statistical law, including its treated-outcome kernel, but remains distinct from the causal full-data extension. The bounds do not match in general, so neither the minimax rate nor a root-\(n\) if-and-only-if elbow is claimed.
gap: Optimal non-root-\(n\) theory for time-varying treatment effects remains open. In this model, the unresolved mathematical issue is the gap between the transition-mediated converse exponent \(r_1=2(\alpha_1+t)/\{2(\alpha_1+t)+d\}\) and the first-order achievable exponent \(\gamma_1+\gamma_t\), together with the analogous terminal-channel gap.
fill: The contribution is an explicit nonmatching bracket: a sample-measurable cross-fitted first-order estimator, a chained fuzzy lower construction pairing \(\pi_1\) with \(g\), the standard terminal fuzzy channel, and a parametric floor. On the fixed rough subclass, the auxiliary law draws \((L_0,L_1,Y^{\rm MAR})\) from \(p_1gK_P\), then applies monotone response indicators with probabilities \(\pi_1(L_0)\) and \(\pi_2(L_1)\). Its observed-data coarsening matches the longitudinal treated-regime coordinates without equating \(L_1\) with \(H_2(1)\).
